content: A common seeding pitfall: seed scripts are treated as a one-time initial-setup step, so when a later migration/feature requires a new default row (e.g. a new config table default), existing already-migrated environments never receive it because the entrypoint only reruns pending schema migrations, not the seed step. Recommended fix is treating small stable reference/default data as part of the migration contract itself (idempotent insert co-located with or immediately following the migration that introduces the table), not as a separate seed script assumed to only run once at genesis.
